findings.title: Negative-offset slicing on Django QuerySet will raise AssertionError, breaking the 'advanced pagination' feature
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly disallows negative start indices (`assert k.start >= 0` / 'Negative indexing is not supported.'), so this will raise an AssertionError at runtime rather than return results. This means the entire advertised 'negative offset for bidirectional pagination' feature will crash with an unhandled exception for any client that actually exercises it, resulting in a 500 error for superusers/org admins using `optimized_pagination=true` with a negative-offset cursor. The feature as implemented does not work and was apparently never exercised against a real QuerySet.

findings.title: Misleading/incorrect comment about Django ORM negative-slice support
findings.body: The comment states 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' and 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level.' Neither claim is accurate: Django does not support negative slicing on querysets (it raises an assertion error), and the comment about permission-safety is irrelevant to the actual bug (the crash described above). Leaving this comment in will mislead future maintainers into believing the negative-offset code path is functional and reviewed, when it is not.

findings.title: Audit-log-specific pagination change applied to shared BasePaginator used by all other endpoints
findings.body: The offset-clamping change (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) was added directly to `BasePaginator.get_result`, which is the base class used by `Paginator` and `DateTimePaginator` across the entire codebase (issues, projects, teams, etc.), not just the audit log endpoint this PR targets. Modifying shared pagination infrastructure for a feature scoped to one experimental endpoint increases blast radius: any subtle behavior change here affects every consumer of `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator`. The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` subclass already exists for isolating this behavior; the shared `BasePaginator` should not need to change for this feature.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates ~90 lines of BasePaginator.get_result instead of extending it
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` copies almost the entirety of `BasePaginator.get_result` logic (cursor handling, hits counting, result trimming, cursor building) with only a small branch added for negative offsets. This duplication means any future bug fix or behavior change made to `BasePaginator.get_result` (e.g., the prev-cursor edge-case handling) will silently diverge from this subclass unless manually kept in sync, creating a maintenance and correctness risk going forward.

findings.title: Direct use of request.user.is_superuser instead of the project's active-superuser check
findings.body: The code gates the 'advanced pagination' feature with `request.user.is_superuser`, which reflects whether the user account has the superuser flag set, not whether the user currently has an active, elevated superuser session. Sentry's security model elsewhere requires verifying active superuser status (e.g. via `is_active_superuser(request)`) before granting elevated behavior, specifically to prevent a superuser-flagged account from getting superuser-level access/features without explicitly entering superuser mode. Using the raw flag here bypasses that intended control for an administrative audit-log feature.

findings.title: Potential AttributeError if organization_context.member is None
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is False. If `organization_context.member` can be `None` for some caller allowed through `OrganizationAuditPermission` (e.g., certain service/API-key or cross-silo contexts), this line will raise an AttributeError resulting in an unhandled 500 instead of a graceful permission denial.

findings.title: No tests added for new OptimizedCursorPaginator or advanced pagination code path
findings.body: This PR introduces a new paginator class (`OptimizedCursorPaginator`) with a non-trivial new negative-offset code path, plus new endpoint logic gating access to it by permission, but no tests were added or updated for either file. Given the negative-offset path is actually broken (see other finding), test coverage would have caught this before merge. Missing tests for the new `optimized_pagination` query parameter branch in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` as well.

findings.title: Comment added without corresponding functional change, is misleading
findings.body: The added comment claims 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios... enables efficient reverse pagination,' but no functional change was made in this file — `self.offset = int(offset)` behaves exactly as before and does not newly 'allow' negative offsets (it always accepted any int, including negative, same as before). The comment implies a capability change that didn't happen here, which can confuse future readers trying to find where 'negative offset support' is actually implemented.
